entries.question: Following up on the text search note, why does grep -F change the results when I search for check.ready?
entries.answer: By default, grep treats the dot as a regular expression character that matches any single character. With -F, grep requires the literal string check.ready. For instance, checkXready matches the regular expression but not the fixed string.

entries.question: How can I count lines that contain a fixed string with grep? What happens if the string appears twice on a line?
entries.answer: Run grep -cF -- 'check.ready' /path/to/example.log. The -c flag counts matching lines, so two matches on the same line count once. If no line matches, grep prints 0 and returns exit status 1. Scripts should distinguish no matches from a read error.
